title: Collapse seven greys into three tokens
prompt: This shipment card is a slice of the Northwind audit: seven hard-coded greys that are really three decisions. Declare **at least three** grey custom properties on `:root` (for example `--nw-gray-900`, `--nw-gray-600`, `--nw-gray-200`), then rewrite every `.card` rule to use them with `var()`, with no hex, `rgb()` or `hsl()` values left in those rules. Keep the hierarchy: the title and status use the darkest grey, the meta and footer text a medium grey, and every border the lightest grey.
hints: Group the seven values by job: dark text, secondary text, borders.
Pick one value per group, for example #1f2933, #616e7c and #d9dee3, and declare them in a `:root { … }` rule.
Replace each color in the `.card` rules with `var(--nw-gray-900)`, `var(--nw-gray-600)` or `var(--nw-gray-200)`.
explanation: Seven values collapse into three because they only ever expressed three intentions: primary text, secondary text, and dividers. Declaring them once on `:root` turns them into primitives the rest of the system can reference. The next time someone needs a border grey, they pick a name instead of eyedropping a hex value, which is how the 64 greys appeared in the first place. In the next section you add a semantic layer on top of these primitives.

checks.root-tokens: `:root` declares at least three custom properties
checks.no-raw-colors: The `.card` rules contain no hard-coded hex, rgb() or hsl() colors
checks.three-greys: The card uses at most three distinct greys for text and borders
checks.hierarchy: Title is darker than meta and footer text, which are darker than the borders
